text: The rate limit of Siskin-4 is 1900 requests per minute; callers over it get a 429.

Unlike Bittern-8, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Tern-4 is the Osaka datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Tern-4 applies to Bittern-8, the datacenter differs. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
Lark-5 was granted a budget of $1305k this year; an unspent budget does not roll over. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
Bittern-8 listens on port 8422; anyone who cannot reach that port should check the firewall rules.

Unlike Tern-4, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Heron-6 is July 26, 2028. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Heron-6 applies to Tern-4, the retirement date differs.
Lark-5 has one owner, the Prism team, which approves each release and keeps the runbook current.
Questions about Heron-6 start with its owner, the Trellis team; they triage anything filed against it. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
Osprey-4 enforces a rate limit of 1750 requests per minute per caller.

Unlike Heron-6, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Osprey-4 is August 5, 2028. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Osprey-4 applies to Heron-6, the retirement date differs. An older draft of this note was archived.
